raw_record.original_question: As shown in the diagram, $AB\parallel CD$, $AC$ bisects $\angle BAD$, $BD$ bisects $\angle ADC$, $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $E$, and $F$, $G$ are moving points on the line segments $AB$ and $AC$, respectively, with $AF=CG$. If $DE=1$ and $AB=2$, what is the minimum value of $DF+DG$?
raw_record.answer:
Solution: Connect BC.\\
Since AC bisects $\angle BAD$ and BD bisects $\angle ADC$, and $AB\parallel CD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DAC=\angle BAC$, $\angle ADB=\angle CDB$, $\angle AED=180^\circ-180^\circ\div2=90^\circ$,\\
Since $AB\parallel CD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DCA=\angle BAC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DCA=\angle DAC$,\\
$\therefore$ $DA=DC$,\\
Similarly: $DA=BA$,\\
$\therefore$ $DC=AB$,\\
Since $AB\parallel CD$,\\
$\therefore$ quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a parallelogram,\\
Since $DA=DC$,\\
$\therefore$ quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rhombus.\\
As shown in the figure, take point $B'$ on $AC$ such that $AB'=AB$, connect $FB'$, construct the symmetric point $D'$ of $D$ about $AB$, and connect $D'F$, $DD'$.\\
Construct $B'H\perp CD$ at point $H$, and construct $B'M\perp DD'$ at point $M$.\\
$\therefore$ $DF=D'F$,\\
Since $AF=CG$, $\angle B'AF=\angle DCG$, $AB'=AB=CD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle B'AF\cong DCG$ (SAS),\\
$\therefore$ $B'F=DG$,\\
$\therefore$ $DF+DG=D'F+B'F$,\\
$\therefore$ when points $B'$, $F$, $D'$ are on the same line, $DF+DG=D'F+B'F$ takes the minimum value of $B'D'$.\\
Since $DE=1$, $AD=AB=2$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DAE=30^\circ$, $\angle ADE=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $AC=\sqrt{3}\,AD=2\sqrt{3}$, $CB'=2\sqrt{3}-2$,\\
$\therefore$ $B'H=\frac{1}{2}B'C=\sqrt{3}-1$, $CH=\sqrt{3}\,B'H=3-\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ $DH=DC-CH=2-(3-\sqrt{3})=\sqrt{3}-1$,\\
Since quadrilateral $DHB'M$ is a rectangle,\\
$\therefore$ $DM=B'H=\sqrt{3}-1$, $MB'=DH=\sqrt{3}-1$,\\
$\therefore$ $D'M=DD'-DM=\sqrt{3}\,AD-(\sqrt{3}-1)=2\sqrt{3}-(\sqrt{3}-1)=\sqrt{3}+1$,\\
$\therefore$ $D'B'=\sqrt{MB'^2+MD'^2}=\sqrt{(\sqrt{3}-1)^2+(\sqrt{3}+1)^2}=2\sqrt{2}$.\\
Therefore, the minimum value of $DF+DG$ is $2\sqrt{2}$.
